# QS-PROC-07 Quench and temper process window (P2)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Scope
- This quality specification defines the acceptable process window for quench and temper operations performed on parts processed on line P2-L2 in plant P2, with emphasis on operations that reference Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01). It establishes requirements, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for process variables and records that determine heat treatment outcome and part integrity. This document applies to finished forgings and to in-process billets that proceed to subsequent machining or assembly operations. Related procedural controls and setup steps are documented in SB-1024, SOP-P2-L2-02, and SOP-P2-L2-04.

Background and rationale
- Heat treating by quench and temper produces microstructure and mechanical properties sensitive to heating uniformity, quench media condition, and tempering profiles. The intent of this specification is to reduce variability originating at the induction heater, quench station, and tempering furnace by identifying critical requirements and inspection points. Equipment-specific considerations for EQ-P2-L2-IH01 are included to ensure lubricant application and heater condition do not compromise surface quality or dimensional stability. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938. Inclusion of lubricant identification allows consistent procurement and application during billet preheat and handling.

Requirements table
- The table below lists process elements, acceptance criteria, rationale, and required records. Acceptance criteria are qualitative where numerical specifications are governed by separate controlled documents; refer to SB-1024 and SOP-P2-L2-02 for measurement procedures.

| Process element | Acceptance criteria | Rationale | Records to keep |
|---|---|---|---|
| Induction heater condition (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) | Heater surfaces clean, intact, and free of deposits; lubricant applied per equipment maintenance reference; visual confirmation of no arcing or smoke during run | Surface condition affects heat transfer uniformity and surface appearance of billets; lubricant selection prevents sticking and minimizes contamination | Equipment maintenance log; visual inspection checklist; lubricant usage record |
| Preheat and soak uniformity | Billet shows no visible thermal gradients or discoloration bands; operator notes uniform coloration and consistent surface appearance across length | Uniform heating is critical to avoid quench distortion and inconsistent microstructure | Process log; operator preheat verification entry |
| Quench medium condition | Quench media clarity and agitation as specified in SOP-P2-L2-04; no visible contamination, foaming, or film at surface | Contaminated or degraded quench medium alters cooling rate and may cause nonuniform hardness or surface defects | Quench media test record; daily media inspection form |
| Tempering stage | Parts exhibit uniform temper color or appearance consistent with reference samples; no temper embrittlement indicators | Tempering restores toughness and relieves residual stress; visual and mechanical indications guide accept/reject | Tempering cycle completion record; temper verification inspection |
| Surface quality after quench | Surface free of quench-related scale, deposits, or fluid retention; any residue removed per cleaning procedure prior to final inspection | Surface defects can mask defects and impede downstream processes | Post-quench cleaning record; final surface inspection report |
| Documentation and traceability | Each heat event documented with unique heat identifier and cross-reference to SB-1024; operator initials and review required | Traceability enables root cause analysis and supplier audits | Heat event log; traceability ledger; sign-off sheet |

Inspection method
- Visual inspection is the primary method for initial acceptance at the induction heater, quench, and temper stages. Inspectors must be trained to recognize the acceptance criteria listed in the requirements table and to use reference samples kept at the line for color and surface condition comparisons. For items where nondestructive testing is specified in SB-1024, inspectors shall follow the method and acceptance criteria in that document. When doubt exists regarding heating uniformity or surface condition, escalate for metallographic cross-sectioning or hardness testing as directed in SOP-P2-L2-02.
- Inspection steps, performed in the sequence below, form the minimum required checks for each heat event:
  - Verify equipment readiness and confirm lubricant CFW-LUB-938 is available and applied per maintenance practice for EQ-P2-L2-IH01.
  - Perform visual verification of billet heating uniformity at the induction heater exit using reference coloration samples.
  - Inspect quench medium condition prior to immersion; document any deviation and do not proceed if contamination or abnormal behavior is observed.
  - After quench, inspect surface condition and ensure cleaning procedures are applied before tempering.
  - During temper, compare part appearance to temper reference samples; document completion and any anomalies.
- Sampling and additional inspection follow the guidance in SB-1024; coordinate with quality engineering if destructive testing is required. Records from each inspection step must be retained in the process log and made available for audit.

Nonconformance handling
- Any condition that fails to meet the acceptance criteria in the requirements table constitutes a nonconformance. Examples include visible heater deposits, quench medium contamination, nonuniform heating signs, or tempering anomalies. Handling steps:
  - Contain affected lots by tagging parts and halting downstream flow until disposition is determined.
  - Notify line supervision and quality engineering immediately, providing heat event identifier and a summary of observed condition.
  - Perform root cause evaluation referencing SB-1024 and SOP-P2-L2-02; include review of maintenance logs for EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and confirmation of lubricant CFW-LUB-938 usage where relevant.
  - If rework is feasible and permitted by specification, define corrective action in writing and record all steps taken. Examples of permissible corrective actions include controlled temper adjustments or surface cleaning when allowed by applicable product specification.
  - When disposition requires scrapping or segregation, record the decision and notify procurement if lubricant or equipment condition contributed to failure.
  - Implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence and document verification activities and effectiveness checks in the process log.
- All nonconformance records shall reference SB-1024 and include links to any applicable work instructions in SOP-P2-L2-02 and SOP-P2-L2-04. Retain nonconformance reports, inspection checklists, and corrective action documentation in the quality system for review during audits.

Records and examples
- Maintain a complete file per heat event containing: heat event log, equipment maintenance log for EQ-P2-L2-IH01, lubricant usage record for CFW-LUB-938, quench media inspection records, temper verification, and any nonconformance reports. Example entries and templates are provided in SOP-P2-L2-02. Records are required for traceability and to support continuous improvement activities outlined in SB-1024.

End of specification.
